name: Lip competence training
lead: Lip competence training is the habit of keeping the lips gently sealed at rest, treated in some oral-posture communities as a posture skill that is said to support jaw and facial development. In orthodontics, lip competence is a clinical descriptor meaning the lips can close at rest without strain, and lip incompetence means they cannot.[2]

A sealed-lip position is also listed as a core element of mewing, alongside tongue posture, lightly touching teeth and nasal breathing.[1] No reviewed study tests whether training lip closure changes facial structure.
infobox: Not directly studied in sources reviewed

paras: Practice guidance in mewing descriptions is to close the lips softly while breathing through the nose.[1] Some practitioners use mouth taping to encourage lip closure during sleep, which a reference article says carries risks and needs professional supervision.[1]

In dentistry and oral surgery, lip competence is a recorded feature of the face. A 1977 report on surgical-orthodontic correction of skeletal open bite lists lip incompetence among indications for the procedure and lip competence among contraindications for a particular type of case.[2] Orthodontic studies also record lip coverage as a variable, for example in a population study of incisor trauma in adolescents that tested for effects of lip coverage among other factors.[3]

No studies found that test lip competence training as an intervention for facial appearance. Clinical literature records lip competence as a feature associated with bite type and dental trauma risk, but that work does not evaluate a training programme.[2][3] 2025 pilot studies of orofacial myofunctional therapy reported effects on hyoid position and jaw pain but did not directly test mewing or lip sealing.[1]

lore.intro: Lip seal is discussed alongside tongue posture and nasal breathing as part of an overall posture routine.

claims.claim: Keeping the lips sealed at rest improves jaw and facial development.
claims.believers: Proponents of orthotropics say a closed mouth and correct oral posture guide growth, and John Mew summarised the basic idea as keeping the mouth shut.[1][4]
claims.experts: The American Association of Orthodontists and the Cleveland Clinic are reported to say there is no credible evidence that mewing reshapes the face.[1] Reviewed orthodontic studies do not test lip-closure training.

card.summary: Keeping the lips sealed at rest as a posture habit; claimed to aid facial growth, untested as training.
card.note: Mouth taping, sometimes used for lip closure, is described as carrying risks.

quick.overview:
Lip competence training means keeping the lips lightly sealed at rest. Some oral-posture communities treat it as part of mewing.

In clinical writing, lip competence is a descriptor of whether lips close at rest. No study tests training it for facial change.
quick.mechanism: Practitioners close the lips softly and breathe through the nose, as part of a routine with tongue posture.
quick.risks: Reference sources say mouth taping used to encourage lip closure carries risks and needs professional supervision.
